label: Yesha'yahu (Isaiah) — 1QIsa-a — Part 1 — Chapters 1–12
summary_plain: Yesha'yahu opens with YHWH's case against Yisra'EL. The ox knows its owner but Yisra'EL does not know. YHWH calls the nation to repentance: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow. Yesha'yahu sees YHWH seated on a high throne — the seraphim cry Holy, holy, holy is YHWH of hosts. A coal touches the prophet's lips. He is sent. The sign of Immanuel is given. The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. A child is born — Wonderful Counselor, Mighty Creator, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
summary_scholarly: The ACR reads from the Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) — the oldest complete prophetic manuscript known, found in Qumran Cave 1. This single scroll preserves all 66 chapters and predates the Masoretic Isaiah by approximately 1,000 years. The Orit Ge'ez serves as the second witness. The throne vision in chapter 6 is the most detailed divine throne description in the prophetic literature. The child of chapters 7 and 9 is a mortal Davidic heir — not a divine incarnation. The Qumran community read these passages as descriptions of a human king in the Davidic line.

key_terms.definition: Prophet of Yehudah during the Assyrian crisis, 8th century BCE; his visions open with YHWH enthroned and the earth filled with divine glory.
Yesha'yahu sees YHWH seated on a high throne in the Temple; seraphim cry 'Holy, holy, holy is YHWH of Hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.'
Fiery celestial beings in the Throne Vision of Yesha'yahu 6; they have six wings and cry the threefold holiness declaration over YHWH's throne.
The threefold acclamation of YHWH's holiness sung by the seraphim in Yesha'yahu 6:3; source text the NT later borrowed from.
Sign given to King Ahaz in Yesha'yahu 7: a young woman will bear a son called Immanuel ('El is with us'); the sign is to Ahaz's immediate historical crisis, not a future figure.
King of Yehudah who refused to ask YHWH for a sign; Yesha'yahu gave the Immanuel sign to the entire House of David in response to Ahaz's faithlessness.
Yesha'yahu 11 describes a future leader who will arise from the severed line of Yishai (David's father); the sevenfold Spirit of YHWH rests on him.
Seven aspects of YHWH's Spirit resting on the coming leader in Yesha'yahu 11: wisdom, understanding, counsel, strength, knowledge, fear of YHWH, and delight in YHWH's fear.
The Great Isaiah Scroll found at Qumran Cave 1; one of the best-preserved DSS manuscripts, containing the entire text of Yesha'yahu with notable textual variants.
The road through the wilderness on which YHWH's redeemed travel; unclean creatures do not walk on it; it appears in Yesha'yahu 35 as part of the restoration vision.

faq.question: What is the 1QIsa-a Scroll and why does it matter?
faq.answer: The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) is the best-preserved manuscript from Qumran, found in Cave 1 in 1947. It contains the full text of Yesha'yahu and predates the Masoretic Text by roughly 1,000 years, preserving textual variants that show the Masoretes' editorial choices—making it an essential pre-Rabbinic witness.

faq.question: Who were the seraphim in Yesha'yahu's Throne Vision?
faq.answer: The seraphim are fiery celestial beings serving in YHWH's throne room. Each has six wings: two covering the face, two covering the feet, two for flying. They continuously cry the threefold holiness declaration over YHWH's throne, their voices shaking the thresholds of the Temple.

faq.question: What was the Immanuel Sign given to Ahaz?
faq.answer: In Yesha'yahu 7, YHWH offered Ahaz any sign as confirmation that YHWH would protect Yehudah. Ahaz refused. YHWH then gave the sign anyway to the entire House of David: a young woman would conceive and bear a son called Immanuel. The sign addressed Ahaz's immediate crisis with Aram and Efrayim.

faq.question: What is the Shoot from Yishai's Stump in Yesha'yahu 11?
faq.answer: After describing Assyria's pride being cut down like a great tree, Yesha'yahu 11 announces that a new shoot will grow from the severed stump of Yishai (David's father). The sevenfold Spirit of YHWH rests on this leader, who rules with wisdom, justice for the poor, and faithfulness.

faq.question: What does the Song of the Vineyard in Yesha'yahu 5 teach?
faq.answer: The Song of the Vineyard (Yesha'yahu 5:1-7) is a parable in which YHWH planted Yisra'el as a beloved vineyard, did everything right, yet it produced wild grapes instead of justice. The punch line: YHWH expected justice (mishpat) and saw bloodshed (mispakh); righteousness (tzedaqah) and heard a cry (tze'aqah).

faq.question: Why is Yesha'yahu 9:6 described as an ancient source text the NT borrowed from?
faq.answer: Yesha'yahu 9:6 — 'For to us a child is born, to us a son is given' — predates the NT by centuries. This ancient Hebrew text is the original; the NT's nativity and 'son given' language borrowed from it. Describing the ancient text as 'NT-like' inverts the chronology.

faq.question: What two Assyrian kings are named in Yesha'yahu 1-12?
faq.answer: Yesha'yahu's ministry covered the reigns of Uziyahu, Yotam, Ahaz, and Khizkiyahu (Yesha'yahu 1:1). The Assyrian kings in this period whose shadow falls over these chapters are Tiglath-Pileser III (called Pul) and Sennakherib. The crisis with Aram-Syria and Efrayim in chapters 7-8 is the Syro-Ephraimitish war.

faq.question: What does the name Immanuel mean?
faq.answer: Immanuel (Hebrew: El-with-us) means 'El is with us.' In Yesha'yahu 7, the name is the sign's message: despite Ahaz's faithlessness, YHWH is still with the House of David. The sign is for the immediate historical crisis, not a promise about a distant future figure.

faq.question: What is the 'Highway of Holiness' in Yesha'yahu 35?
faq.answer: Yesha'yahu 35:8 describes a Way of Holiness through the wilderness on which YHWH's redeemed travel from exile back to Tziyon. It is so pure that even the unwise cannot stray from it, and unclean creatures do not walk on it. The redeemed come back to Tziyon with singing and everlasting joy.

faq.question: What sin did Yesha'yahu confess in the Throne Vision?
faq.answer: When he saw YHWH enthroned, Yesha'yahu cried 'Woe is me! I am undone; for I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips.' A seraph then flew to him with a burning coal from the altar and touched his mouth, declaring his guilt taken away and his sin atoned.
